title: “And how, monks, is a monk called an arahant? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing…
content: “And how, monks, is a monk called an arahant? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is an arahant.”

title: “Monks, when the child grows up and his faculties become mature, he enjoys the five strands of sensual pleasure fully: forms cognizable by the eye…
content: “Monks, when the child grows up and his faculties become mature, he enjoys the five strands of sensual pleasure fully: forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing; sounds cognizable by the ear … odors cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … tangibles cognizable by the body that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. When he sees a form with the eye, he lusts after a pleasing form and dislikes a displeasing form. He dwells with mindfulness not established on the body, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom where those evil, unwholesome states cease without remainder. Thus, in relation to the body, whichever feeling arises — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — he delights in that feeling, welcomes it, and clings to it. Because he delights, welcomes, and clings, delight in sensual pleasure arises. With delight in sensual pleasure, there is clinging. With clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: Suffering from disease and aging, And also subject to death — Such is the nature of conditioned things, Such is the nature of beings. If…
content:
Suffering from disease and aging,
And also subject to death —
Such is the nature of conditioned things,
Such is the nature of beings.
If ordinary people become disenchanted,
That would not be fitting for me —
If I too were disenchanted
With beings who share the same fate.
While I live,
Not different from them,
I dwell thus,
Knowing the Dhamma without attachment.
Conceit in health,
In youth, in life —
All these I have subdued,
Springing from security.
I see the path of seclusion,
I arouse strong energy,
Seeing the state of Nibbāna.
Now I cannot
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
I will not fall back,
Achieving the final goal of the holy life.

title: Elder Rāhula: Blinded by sensual desires, Covered by the net of wrong views, Craving acts as a veil, Covering, hiding completely. Bound by heedlessness, Like…
content:
Elder Rāhula:

Blinded by sensual desires,
Covered by the net of wrong views,
Craving acts as a veil,
Covering, hiding completely.
Bound by heedlessness,
Like a fish caught in a net.

I have overcome those sensual desires,
Cut Māra’s bondage.
Having pulled out the root of craving,
I am cooled, at peace.

title: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
content: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, there is an establishment of consciousness. When consciousness is established and grows, there is a production of future renewed existence. When there is future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: "When the eye sees a form, the monk does not grasp the general feature, does not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the…
content: "When the eye sees a form, the monk does not grasp the general feature, does not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — that cause the monk restrains, guards the eye faculty... By means of this noble restraint of the faculties, he experiences an internal feeling of ease, unblemished."

title: “Fletchers make arrows, Potters make pots, Carpenters shape wood, The wise tame themselves.” “Like a solid rock Unmoved by the wind, So the wise are…
content:
“Fletchers make arrows,
Potters make pots,
Carpenters shape wood,
The wise tame themselves.”

“Like a solid rock
Unmoved by the wind,
So the wise are unmoved
Amid praise and blame.”

“Like a deep lake,
Clear, unruffled,
So the wise become serene,
Hearing the Dhamma.”

“The good renounce everything,
The virtuous do not prattle about sensual desires.
Whether touched by pleasure or pain,
The wise show neither elation nor depression.”

title: “Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely…
content: “Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely the four great elements and form derived from the four great elements. Thus, monks, a monk does not know forms. Monks, how is a monk one who is not skillful in characteristics? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is the fool and the characteristics of a fool, the wise person and the characteristics of a wise person. Thus, monks, a monk is not skillful in characteristics. Monks, how is a monk one who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly? Here, monks, a monk indulges in arisen sensual thoughts; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. He indulges in arisen ill-will thoughts … harmful thoughts … evil, unwholesome states that have arisen; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. Thus, monks, is a monk who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly.”

title: “Abandon desire, abandon greed — These are the bonds of worldlings. The one with eyes walks the path, Crosses hell and human birth. Eating little,…
content:
“Abandon desire, abandon greed —
These are the bonds of worldlings.
The one with eyes walks the path,
Crosses hell and human birth.

Eating little, moderate in food,
With few wishes, not greedy —
He is without desire, without craving,
Truly at peace.

Having gone on alms-round,
The sage enters the forest,
Goes to the root of a tree,
Prepares his sitting place.

The wise one, meditating,
Delights in the forest,
Meditating at the root of a tree,
Content, he practices his own pleasure.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as unwise attention. For one who…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as unwise attention. For one who attends unwisely, monks, unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline.”
